## sed-inplace-no-suffix

**`sed -i` without a backup suffix** · breaks on macOS · error

GNU sed treats the suffix of -i as optional and attached (`-i.bak`). BSD sed (macOS) always consumes the next argument as the suffix, so `sed -i s/a/b/ file` fails, and `sed -i -e ...` silently leaves backup files named `file-e`.

**Fix:** Attach a suffix and remove the backup: `sed -i.bak ... file && rm -f file.bak` works everywhere.

```sh
# breaks
sed -i 's/hello/bye/' f.txt && cat f.txt

# portable
sed -i.bak 's/hello/bye/' f.txt && rm -f f.txt.bak && cat f.txt
```

## sed-inplace-empty-suffix

**`sed -i ''` (BSD form)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

On GNU and BusyBox sed the empty string after -i is read as the script, so `sed -i '' s/a/b/ file` fails with "can't read s/a/b/".

**Fix:** Use `sed -i.bak ... file && rm -f file.bak`, which both implementations accept.

```sh
# breaks
sed -i '' 's/hello/bye/' f.txt && cat f.txt

# portable
sed -i.bak 's/hello/bye/' f.txt && rm -f f.txt.bak && cat f.txt
```

## sed-gnu-flags

**GNU-only sed options** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD sed has no long options (`--expression`, `--regexp-extended`, `--quiet`, `--in-place`...) and no `-s` or `-z`.

**Fix:** Use the short forms: `-e`, `-E`, `-n`, and `-i.bak`. For NUL-separated input use `tr` or `perl -0pe`.

```sh
# breaks
sed --expression='s/hello/bye/' f.txt

# portable
sed -e 's/hello/bye/' f.txt
```

## sed-gnu-escapes

**GNU regex escapes in sed (`\s`, `\w`)** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD sed does not understand `\s`, `\S`, `\w` or `\W`. They silently match nothing, so the substitution does not happen and no error is printed.

**Fix:** Use POSIX classes: `[[:space:]]`, `[^[:space:]]`, `[[:alnum:]_]`, `[^[:alnum:]_]`.

```sh
# breaks
echo 'a b' | sed 's/\s/_/'

# portable
echo 'a b' | sed 's/[[:space:]]/_/'
```

## sed-oneline-aic

**One-line `a`, `i`, `c` commands in sed** · breaks on macOS · error

GNU sed accepts `sed "/x/a text"` and `sed "1i text"`. BSD sed requires a backslash and a real newline after the command letter and rejects the one-line form with "expected \ after a, c or i".

**Fix:** Put the text on its own line after `a\`, or use `awk`/`printf` to build the output.

```sh
# breaks
printf 'x\n' | sed '1i hello'

# portable
printf 'x\n' | sed '1i\
hello'
```

## sed-step-address

**GNU sed address forms (`first~step`, `addr,+N`)** · breaks on macOS · error

The `first~step`, `addr,+N`, `addr,~N` and `0,/re/` addresses are GNU extensions. BSD sed reports an unknown command.

**Fix:** Use `awk` (`NR % 2 == 1`) or restructure with line numbers.

```sh
# breaks
printf '1\n2\n3\n' | sed -n '1~2p'

# portable
printf '1\n2\n3\n' | awk 'NR % 2 == 1'
```

## grep-perl-regexp

**`grep -P` (Perl regex)** · breaks on macOS, Alpine · error

BSD grep (macOS) and BusyBox grep (Alpine) do not implement `-P`. Scripts that parse output with `grep -oP` are the most common portability failure on macOS.

**Fix:** Use `grep -E` with POSIX classes, or `sed -n "s/.../\1/p"`. For lookaround use `perl -ne` or `awk`.

```sh
# breaks
echo abc | grep -oP 'b\w'

# portable
echo abc | grep -oE 'b[[:alnum:]_]'
```

## find-gnu-primaries

**GNU-only `find` primaries** · breaks on macOS · error

`-printf`, `-regextype`, `-executable`, `-readable`, `-writable` and `-xtype` do not exist in BSD find. `-printf` is also missing from BusyBox find.

**Fix:** Use `-exec basename {} \;` / `-exec stat ... {} +` instead of `-printf`, and `-perm` instead of `-executable`.

```sh
# breaks
find . -maxdepth 1 -name f.txt -printf '%f\n'

# portable
find . -maxdepth 1 -name f.txt -exec basename {} \;
```

## find-bsd-regex-flag

**`find -E` (BSD extended regex)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

BSD find takes `-E` before the path to enable extended regular expressions. GNU and BusyBox find do not know the option.

**Fix:** Use `-name`/`-path` globs, or filter with `grep -E`: `find . | grep -E "..."`.

```sh
# breaks
find -E . -maxdepth 1 -regex '.*/f\.txt'

# portable
find . -maxdepth 1 -name 'f.txt'
```

## xargs-delimiter

**`xargs -d`** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD xargs has no `-d` / `--delimiter`.

**Fix:** Use `tr` to convert the delimiter to newlines (`tr "," "\n" | xargs ...`) or `-0` with NUL-separated input.

```sh
# breaks
printf 'a b' | xargs -d ' ' echo

# portable
printf 'a b' | tr ' ' '\n' | xargs echo
```

## xargs-replace-J

**`xargs -J` (BSD)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

`-J replstr` is a BSD xargs option; GNU and BusyBox xargs only know `-I`.

**Fix:** Use `xargs -I % ...`, which BSD, GNU and BusyBox all accept.

```sh
# breaks
printf 'a\n' | xargs -J % echo % x

# portable
printf 'a\n' | xargs -I % echo % x
```

## awk-gawk-extensions

**gawk-only functions in awk** · breaks on macOS · error

macOS ships the one-true-awk. It lacks `gensub`, `strftime`, `systime`, `mktime`, `asort`, `asorti`, `strtonum` and `-i inplace`; calling them is a fatal "undefined function". BusyBox awk lacks most of them too.

**Fix:** Use `gsub`, `date`, `sort`, or `printf "%d"` in POSIX awk, or install gawk explicitly and call it as `gawk`.

```sh
# breaks
awk 'BEGIN{print strtonum("0x10")}'

# portable
printf '%d\n' 0x10
```

## gnu-long-options

**GNU long options on BSD tools** · breaks on macOS · error

Most BSD utilities on macOS (cp, mv, rm, mkdir, ln, du, df, cut, wc, touch, chmod, ps, ...) accept only short flags. `rm --force` fails with "illegal option -- -".

**Fix:** Use the short flag equivalent (see the per-command hint in the message).

```sh
# breaks
cp --force f.txt g.txt && cat g.txt

# portable
cp -f f.txt g.txt && cat g.txt
```

## date-gnu-flags

**`date -d` and other GNU date options** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD date has no `-d`, `--date` or `--iso-8601`. It parses dates with `-j -f FORMAT` and does arithmetic with `-v`.

**Fix:** There is no single portable flag. Branch on `uname`, or use `date -u -r SECONDS` (BSD) with `date -u -d @SECONDS` (GNU, BusyBox) as a fallback.

```sh
# breaks
date -u -d '2020-01-02 03:04:05' +%Y

# portable
date -u -r 1577934245 +%Y 2>/dev/null || date -u -d @1577934245 +%Y
```

## date-bsd-flags

**`date -v` / `date -j` (BSD)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

`-v` (adjust) and `-j -f` (parse) are BSD date options; GNU date and BusyBox date reject them.

**Fix:** Branch on `uname`, or use `date -u -d` on GNU and `date -u -v` on BSD behind a check.

```sh
# breaks
date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' '2020-01-02 03:04:05' +%Y

# portable
date -u -r 1577934245 +%Y 2>/dev/null || date -u -d @1577934245 +%Y
```

## stat-gnu-format

**`stat -c` / `--format`** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD stat formats with `-f` and uses different specifiers; `-c`, `--format`, `--printf` and `--terse` do not exist.

**Fix:** For a size use `wc -c < file`. For other fields branch on `uname`.

```sh
# breaks
stat -c %s f.txt

# portable
wc -c < f.txt | tr -d ' '
```

## stat-bsd-format

**`stat -f FORMAT` (BSD)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

On GNU stat and BusyBox stat, `-f` means "filesystem status", not "format", so `stat -f %z file` prints filesystem data or fails.

**Fix:** For a size use `wc -c < file`. For other fields branch on `uname`.

```sh
# breaks
stat -f %z f.txt

# portable
wc -c < f.txt | tr -d ' '
```

## head-negative-count

**`head -n -N` (all but the last N lines)** · breaks on macOS · error

Negative line counts are a GNU extension. BSD head fails with "illegal line count".

**Fix:** Use `sed "$d"` to drop the last line, or `awk` to drop the last N.

```sh
# breaks
printf 'a\nb\n' | head -n -1

# portable
printf 'a\nb\n' | sed '$d'
```

## du-apparent-bytes

**`du -b`** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD du has no `-b` (apparent size in bytes).

**Fix:** Use `wc -c < file` for one file, or `find ... -exec wc -c {} +`.

```sh
# breaks
du -b f.txt | cut -f1

# portable
wc -c < f.txt | tr -d ' '
```

## ln-gnu-flags

**`ln -r` / `ln -T`** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD ln has no `--relative` (`-r`) or `--no-target-directory` (`-T`).

**Fix:** Create the link from the directory it lives in with a relative target: `(cd dir && ln -s ../target name)`.

```sh
# breaks
ln -s -r f.txt l && cat l

# portable
ln -s f.txt l && cat l
```

## install-create-dirs

**`install -D`** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD install has no `-D` to create leading directories.

**Fix:** Run `mkdir -p "$(dirname dest)"` first, then `install`.

```sh
# breaks
install -D f.txt out/sub/f.txt && echo ok

# portable
mkdir -p out/sub && install f.txt out/sub/f.txt && echo ok
```

## touch-relative-date

**`touch -d` with a relative date** · breaks on macOS · error

BSD touch accepts `-d` only with an ISO-8601 timestamp, not strings like "2 days ago" or "yesterday".

**Fix:** Use `touch -t YYYYMMDDhhmm` or compute the timestamp with `date`.

```sh
# breaks
touch -d '2 days ago' f.txt && echo ok

# portable
touch -t 202001010000 f.txt && echo ok
```

## mktemp-t-prefix

**`mktemp -t prefix` (BSD)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

On BSD, `-t prefix` builds a name from a prefix. GNU and BusyBox mktemp require a template ending in `XXXXXX` and fail with "too few X's in template".

**Fix:** Pass a full template: `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/prefix.XXXXXX"`.

```sh
# breaks
mktemp -t foo >/dev/null && echo ok

# portable
mktemp -t foo.XXXXXX >/dev/null && echo ok
```

## getopt-long-options

**external `getopt` with long options** · breaks on macOS · error

macOS ships the legacy BSD `getopt`, which ignores `-l`/`--long` and `-o`. The parsed result is silently wrong.

**Fix:** Use the `getopts` shell builtin, or a manual `while case` loop for long options.

```sh
# breaks
getopt -o a -l long -- --long

# portable
echo "--long --"
```

## tail-reverse

**`tail -r` (BSD)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

`tail -r` (print lines in reverse) exists on BSD only. GNU has `tac`, which macOS lacks.

**Fix:** Use the POSIX `sed '1!G;h;$!d'`.

```sh
# breaks
printf 'a\nb\n' | tail -r

# portable
printf 'a\nb\n' | sed '1!G;h;$!d'
```

## base64-decode-D

**`base64 -D` (BSD)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

BSD base64 spells decode `-D`. GNU and BusyBox use `-d`, and so do current macOS releases.

**Fix:** Use `base64 -d`. For wrapping control use `tr -d "\n"`; `-w` is GNU-only.

```sh
# breaks
printf 'aGk=' | base64 -D

# portable
printf 'aGk=' | base64 -d
```

## sysctl-bsd-keys

**`sysctl hw.*` (BSD keys)** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

Keys such as `hw.ncpu` or `machdep.cpu.brand_string` only exist on BSD/macOS. On Linux `sysctl` reads `/proc/sys` and fails.

**Fix:** Use `getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN` for the CPU count, or branch on `uname`.

```sh
# breaks
sysctl -n hw.ncpu >/dev/null && echo ok

# portable
getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN >/dev/null && echo ok
```

## bash4-mapfile

**`mapfile` / `readarray` need bash 4** · breaks on macOS · warn

macOS still ships bash 3.2 as /bin/bash (and `#!/usr/bin/env bash` finds it unless Homebrew bash is first in PATH). `mapfile` and `readarray` were added in bash 4.0.

**Fix:** Read lines in a loop: `while IFS= read -r line; do arr+=("$line"); done < <(command)`.

```sh
# breaks
mapfile -t arr < <(printf 'a\nb\n'); echo ${#arr[@]}

# portable
while IFS= read -r l; do arr+=("$l"); done < <(printf 'a\nb\n'); echo ${#arr[@]}
```

## bash4-associative-array

**associative arrays need bash 4** · breaks on macOS · warn

`declare -A` (also `local -A`, `typeset -A`) was added in bash 4.0; bash 3.2 reports "invalid option".

**Fix:** Use two parallel indexed arrays, a `case` statement, or a temp file of `key=value` lines.

```sh
# breaks
declare -A m && m[a]=1 && m[b]=2 && echo "${m[a]}"
```

## bash4-nameref

**namerefs (`declare -n`) need bash 4.3** · breaks on macOS · warn

`declare -n` / `local -n` namerefs were added in bash 4.3.

**Fix:** Use `eval` with a validated variable name, or return values via stdout.

```sh
# breaks
f(){ local -n r=$1; r=ok; }; f v; echo "$v"
```

## bash4-case-modification

**`${var,,}` / `${var^^}` need bash 4** · breaks on macOS · warn

Case-modifying parameter expansion was added in bash 4.0; bash 3.2 fails with "bad substitution".

**Fix:** Use `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'` (or the reverse).

```sh
# breaks
v=AbC; echo "${v,,}"

# portable
v=AbC; echo "$v" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'
```

## bash4-negative-index

**`${arr[-1]}` needs bash 4.3** · breaks on macOS · warn

Negative array subscripts were added in bash 4.3; bash 3.2 fails with "bad array subscript".

**Fix:** Compute the index: `${arr[${#arr[@]}-1]}`.

```sh
# breaks
a=(x y); echo "${a[-1]}"

# portable
a=(x y); echo "${a[${#a[@]}-1]}"
```

## bash4-redirect-append-both

**`&>>` and `|&` need bash 4** · breaks on macOS · warn

Both operators were added in bash 4.0 and are syntax errors in bash 3.2.

**Fix:** Write `>> file 2>&1` and `2>&1 |`.

```sh
# breaks
echo x &>> out.txt; cat out.txt

# portable
echo x >> out.txt 2>&1; cat out.txt
```

## bash4-globstar

**`shopt -s globstar` needs bash 4** · breaks on macOS · warn

The `globstar` shell option (`**` matches recursively) was added in bash 4.0.

**Fix:** Use `find . -name "*.ext"` instead of `**/*.ext`.

```sh
# breaks
shopt -s globstar && echo ok
```

## bash4-wait-n

**`wait -n` needs bash 4.3** · breaks on macOS · warn

`wait -n` (wait for any job) was added in bash 4.3.

**Fix:** Poll with `kill -0 $pid` or wait for specific pids.

```sh
# breaks
sleep 0.1 & wait -n && echo ok
```

## bash4-test-v

**`[[ -v var ]]` needs bash 4.2** · breaks on macOS · warn

The `-v` variable-is-set test was added in bash 4.2.

**Fix:** Use `[[ -n "${var+x}" ]]`, which also works in bash 3.2.

```sh
# breaks
x=1; [[ -v x ]] && echo ok

# portable
x=1; [[ -n "${x+x}" ]] && echo ok
```

## bash5-epoch-variables

**`$EPOCHSECONDS` / `$EPOCHREALTIME` need bash 5** · breaks on macOS · warn

These variables were added in bash 5.0 and expand to nothing in bash 3.2.

**Fix:** Use `date +%s`.

```sh
# breaks
[ -n "$EPOCHSECONDS" ] && echo ok

# portable
[ -n "$(date +%s)" ] && echo ok
```

## sh-echo-escapes

**`echo -e` in a POSIX sh script** · breaks on macOS, Linux · warn

Under `/bin/sh` the `-e` flag is not portable: macOS sh and Debian/Ubuntu dash print a literal `-e`. It only works in bash, zsh and BusyBox ash.

**Fix:** Use `printf` with a format string: `printf "a\tb\n"`.

```sh
# breaks
echo -e 'a\tb'

# portable
printf 'a\tb\n'
```

## homebrew-gnu-prefix

**Homebrew-style `g`-prefixed GNU tools** · breaks on Linux, Alpine · error

Names like `gsed`, `gdate` and `gtar` only exist where Homebrew installed GNU coreutils, findutils, sed, grep or tar. They are missing on Linux, Alpine and on a stock Mac.

**Fix:** Pick the binary once: `if command -v gsed >/dev/null 2>&1; then SED=gsed; else SED=sed; fi`, then call `"$SED"`.
